sourceOccurrences.label: Connection distance and its directional limit
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Complete grouped source-contract exposition with explicit additional applications
sourceOccurrences.note: NZMZ uses the extended convention minus log zero = infinity; 8TZJ gives the symmetric triangle inequality from Harris. K2LV retains countability, an Abelian group, translation invariance of the two-point function and positivity along every positive multiple. The infimum bound itself needs neither invariance nor Harris. Real-log helpers at zero use totalized conventions, not the extended distance. The all-open witness has zero rate. I8WP and 23RT are additional deductions from lattice path counts and a direct long bond respectively, not source exports. Positive small-parameter lattice rate is not extended to the entire subcritical phase.

proofUses.reason: Positive association and concatenation imply the multiplicative two-point inequality; negative logarithms give the triangle inequality.
Translation invariance converts the triangle inequality into subadditivity along the direction.
The directional limit, path-count growth and lattice metric turn the tail of the open-path sum into a positive exponential rate.
The direct long bond forces zero exponential rate; summability of the power kernel and the intensity row estimate give finite small-intensity susceptibility.
Subadditivity, integer homogeneity and Lipschitz extension give a seminorm. A finite rational directional net upgrades directional limits to a uniform error bound.
Finite-range exponential radius decay gives a positive lower bound on the norm. Sharpness supplies finite susceptibility throughout the nearest-neighbour subcritical phase.

The first-exit inequality gives a convolution with a contracting bounded-support kernel. Finite iteration and support bounds yield spatial exponential decay; directional limits give the length comparison.
A definition; it invokes no other wiki assertion.
